mutations.because: HL-D8's gap was the markup ignoring tone and hard-coding "bold" while the canvas derived weight from it. Reverting the assembler's default weight to the old literal reopens exactly that gap: a "subtle" variant would ship heavier markup than its own raster fallback, silently, because nothing else in the pipeline notices a font-weight mismatch between the two renderers.

This is the regression the orchestrator's fix round closes: the markup positions text with CSS flex `justify-content`, which must follow the element's own anchor (`top`/`middle`/`bottom`) for the browser to lay out the right side of the box regardless of how many lines the text wraps to. A `justify-content` that no longer follows the anchor renders every text element flush to the top of its frame — a `bottom`-anchored headline (or a `middle`-anchored one) would render in the wrong place with nothing else in the pipeline noticing, the same "looks fine in review" shape as the padding-top regression this replaces.

Qodo finding: htmlWeightReading must measure every distinct tone the draft will actually generate a bundle for, not just the first one — generation writes one html unit per treatment (brief mode) or per variant (variation mode), and each carries its own tone. Measuring only the first tone reopens exactly the gap just closed: a later bold treatment (or a tone-axis value ordered after the first) can produce a larger bundle than the one the meter reports, so an over-budget unit ships without the editor ever warning about it.
